subject: Production throttling — HelioCare: rate-window mismatch and exec intervention requested
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@heliocare.io>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Ramesh <priya@heliocare.io>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:06 -0700
Subject: Sudden 503/429 spikes — impacting patient ingestion (prod)

Neha —

We started seeing a surge of 503s and 429s for our production ingest pipeline starting ~08:55 PT. Latency for the same calls jumped from ~120ms to 2–4s, then dropped to 0 responses (503). Attached is a screenshot from our SLO dashboard and a small sample of request logs. This is affecting a handful of customer flows and paging our on-call.

Can you confirm if this is a tenant-side rate limit, quota, or something on Redwood's end? We are on the reserved tier (HLCARE-8472). This is urgent — can you escalate to ops/execs if needed?

Attachments: helio-sla-screenshot-503.png, prod-logs-20270301.csv

Thanks,
Samir
Customer Success / HelioCare
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@heliocare.io>
Cc: Priya Ramesh <priya@heliocare.io>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:34:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden 503/429 spikes — impacting patient ingestion (prod)

Samir — thanks for the quick report and the attachments. We’re looking now.

Quick status: I’ve opened ticket INF-5321 and forwarded logs to infra. Initial signs point at rate-window enforcement hitting HelioCare’s tenant tokens because of a burst pattern in a narrow time window — it’s causing the safety valve to engage and cascade 503s. I don’t have the full RCA yet.

I will:
- Escalate to the on-call infra team and engineering lead (internal).
- Request temporary guardrail adjustment while we investigate.
- Schedule an exec sync if we need a customer-facing SLA exception.

Please share any additional request traces you can drop in the ticket. I’ll update in 30–45 minutes.

— Neha
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 10:05:15 -0700
Subject: HelioCare — immediate exec attention recommended (rate-window mismatch)

Marissa / Monica / Jonas —

Forwarding customer report (below). Quick summary of my read from logs: HelioCare has a narrow burst of high-concurrency DM requests starting 08:55 PT; their tenant-level token-bucket burned through burst credits in ~45s which then triggered global safety valve (we cap per-tenant burst window to avoid overload). That safety valve dropped requests to 429, then some upstream worker retries escalated to 503s.

Why this is exec-worthy: HelioCare is a Reserved customer (committed capacity). The tenant-level burst window and the global guardrail aren’t aligned for their workload pattern; the result is an unexpected customer-facing outage and a potential SLA hit. They’re in a high-priority pilot for an enterprise payer.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: can you authorize a temporary burst-window increase or guardrail relaxation for HelioCare in us-west-2 for the next 2 hours? We’ll monitor and roll back after.
- Jonas: ops/infra to push safe override + patch quick metric to avoid re-triggering on the same pattern.
- Monica: please prep exec note + one-pager for the CRO and the HelioCare CTO (Alice Ng). I’ve attached the MAP draft for sign-off.

Attachments: MAP-HelioCare-20270301.docx, prod-logs-20270301.csv

Neha
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 10:20:40 -0700
Subject: Re: HelioCare — immediate exec attention recommended (rate-window mismatch)

+1 — I authorize a temporary guardrail relaxation for HelioCare in us-west-2: increase tenant burst window by 25% and increase burst-credit threshold for 2 hours. Ops: implement now and monitor error rates & latency closely. If any signs of backend instability, revert immediately.

Monica: loop in Sarah in Legal if we need to commit a short SLA carve-out. Jonas: coordinate with infra and confirm when done.

Marissa
VP, Customer Success
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 13:45:03 -0700
Subject: Re: HelioCare — immediate exec attention recommended (rate-window mismatch)

Done. What we executed:
- Pushed tenant-specific override: burst_window_us = 60s -> 75s for tenant hlcare-prod, applied to us-west-2 edge cluster at 13:18 PT.
- Increased burst-credit cap by +25% for 2 hours.
- Added a short-circuit to reject client retries that happen inside the safety valve to prevent retry storms.

Observed impact: 429 rate dropped from ~12% -> 0.4% over 20 minutes; 503s subsided after we broke the retry spiral. Latency back to baseline ~140ms median.

Quick root cause (short): the tenant has a periodic fanout job that spikes concurrency for a narrow window — our global guardrail assumes smoothing over a 5m window, while tenant burst was concentrated under 1m. The mismatch (windowing + token-bucket sizing) produced token starvation.

Logs snippet:
"hlcare-prod | 2027-03-01T08:55:23Z | tok_bucket=0 | incoming=1120rps | 429_count=342"
"hlcare-prod | 2027-03-01T08:56:05Z | tok_bucket=0 | retry=120 -> upstream 503s"

Next steps I’m tracking:
- Engineering: propose a policy change to allow conservative automatic per-tenant temporary relief when committed capacity is detected. (INF-5389)
- Product: review documentation to call out this pattern for Dedicated/Reserved customers.
- CS: align with customer on a post-mortem + prevent recurrence (backfill smoother or staggered fanout).

Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@heliocare.io>, Priya Ramesh <priya@heliocare.io>, Alice Ng <alice@heliocare.io>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 16:45:10 -0700
Subject: Update: HelioCare production error spike — mitigation complete and next steps

Hi Samir / Priya / Alice —

Summary and timeline: we saw a concentrated burst of high concurrency at ~08:55 PT which exhausted tenant burst credits and triggered a global safety valve. That produced a short window of 429s and some cascading 503s from upstream retries. Our infra team implemented a temporary guardrail relaxation and a retry short-circuit; both mitigations were applied at ~13:18 PT and we observed error rates drop to baseline within ~20 minutes.

What we did for you:
- Temporary burst-window increase and +25% burst-credit cap for hlcare-prod in us-west-2 (2-hour window).
- Short-circuit to limit retry amplification inside the safety valve.
- Collected logs and a short MAP (attached) and opened INF-5321 & INF-5389 for follow-up policy work.

Attachments: MAP-HelioCare-20270301.docx, prod-logs-20270301.csv

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick post-mortem with HelioCare (30–45m) tomorrow to review the fanout schedule and adjust client-side pacing.
2) Product/Engineering will propose a policy change to automatically detect committed/reserved tenants and allow conservative temporary relief to avoid SLA impact.
3) CS to review a one-time SLA carve-out if HelioCare needs credits; Marissa will advise.

I’m available for a call now if you prefer live — otherwise, we can plan the post-mortem for tomorrow.

Thanks for your patience and apologies for the disruption.

— Neha
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
